where: infernal-lance · Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos · Consumed with Hunger
why: The ability is printed with the (Aura) label in all three sources: Wahapedia datasheet “Consumed with Hunger (Aura): While a friendly WAR DOG model is within 6" …”, New Recruit “Consumed with Hunger (Aura)”, BSData “Consumed with Hunger (Aura)”.

where: infernal-lance · Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos · Consumed with Hunger
why: The ability only works for “a friendly WAR DOG model”. None of the six units in armyUnits has WAR DOG (four Knights are Cerastus/Abhorrent TITANIC, plus the Nurglings), and nothing in the Infernal Lance detachment makes a non-WAR DOG unit count as one or be affected by WAR DOG auras. The two rules that would (Masters of the Pack and Throne Tyrannicus, both Helhunt Lance) and A Long Leash (Traitoris Lance) are not in this list. So the mark is certain. It is a fact about the list, not a reading of the rule, and the ability stays on the datasheet with its text, so it is marked rather than hidden. This matches the precedent (“No VEHICLE in this list”, Thundercharge on the Knight lists).

where: infernal-lance · Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos · Knight Diabolus
why: An Infernal Lance enhancement (Wahapedia “Knight Diabolus 25 pts”). NR gives it to the Atrapos: “Options: Knight Diabolus, Atrapos lascutter, …”.

“Each time this model makes an attack that targets a MONSTER or VEHICLE unit, add 1 to the Hit roll.” The footnote covers all attacks with +1 to hit vs MONSTER/VEHICLE. Being always on, keyed to the hand-set target's keywords, is the owner's Damage-tab convention.

“If that target is TITANIC or TOWERING, add 1 to the Wound roll as well.” “That target” is the MONSTER or VEHICLE target of the first sentence, so vs any TITANIC/TOWERING also requiring MONSTER/VEHICLE is exactly the text. +1 to wound is literal.

“While the bearer is using the Diabolic Power ability, its melee weapons have the [LANCE] ability.” The footnote is melee only, and its condition is Diabolic Power (a Malefic Surge ability). The WS +1 part is already in the profiles (NR prints WS 2+; the datasheet has 3+), as data.js says.

“While this model has 1-10 wounds remaining, subtract 5 from this model’s Objective Control characteristic and each time this model makes an attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll.” The footnote has the band, -1 to hit on all attacks, and -5 OC. The same item covers the Atrapos (identical text).

The aura is for WAR DOG units, within 6" of the Atrapos, vs TITANIC or TOWERING, and gives “you can re-roll the Hit roll”. It is literal. It applies to no unit here (no WAR DOG), which is consistent with the na mark.

NR: “1x Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos — Atrapos lascutter, Graviton singularity cannon”. The ranged profiles are lascutter low/high intensity and graviton contained/singularity, and the melee profiles are lascutter low/high intensity. The datasheet says “equipped with: Atrapos lascutter; graviton singularity cannon”.

The re-roll and the target tick are fine. The fix keeps the shape and adds the reselection in the text's words.

fix.when: Target is its victim (selected at the start of the first battle round, and a new one each time its victim is destroyed)

why: The aura matches the app's text (NR and BSData): “each time that War Dog model makes an attack that targets the closest enemy unit, improve the Armour Penetration … by 1”, which gives “target is the closest enemy unit”. Wahapedia's Knight Ruinator datasheet reads differently: “each time that WAR DOG model makes an attack that targets the closest eligible target”. Reading 1 (NR/BSData): the closest enemy unit, whether or not it can be targeted. Reading 2 (Wahapedia, the 11th-ed wording of the core rules' “closest eligible target” example): the closest unit the War Dog could target. No deviation records the difference, and the GW pack does not print the Ruinator's abilities. Nothing in play depends on it here (no WAR DOG), but the owner should pick the source wording, or mark the disagreement (srcNote), before both this and the ability text are signed off.

NR and Wahapedia: darkflame lance, terrorpulse missiles, and fellbore (strike and sweep). The profiles match the pack's Rules Updates: “Darkflame Lance [IGNORES COVER, TORRENT] 18" D6+6 N/A 8 -1 2” and “Terrorpulse Missiles [BLAST] 36" D6+6 3+ 8 -2 2”.
“Each time an enemy unit … within Engagement Range of one or more units with this ability is selected to fight”. That is the Fight phase, in either player's turn.

NR prints “Mischief Makers (Aura)”, and BSData (Chaos Daemons Library) has “Mischief Makers (Aura)”. Wahapedia's datasheet prints the name without the label, a minor source difference. Two sources, including the owner's export, carry it, so the tag quotes a label and adds nothing.

“Each time an enemy unit (excluding TITANIC units) within Engagement Range … is selected to fight, until the end of the phase, each time a model in that enemy unit makes a melee attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll.” The When targeted line keeps the TITANIC exclusion, the Engagement Range condition, melee only and the duration. Any enemy melee attack on the Nurglings is made from within Engagement Range, so the line is right for the unit itself.
NR: “3x Nurgling Swarm — Diseased claws and teeth”, printed “Diseased claws and teeth (x3)”. Wahapedia: “Every model is equipped with: diseased claws and teeth.” ×3 for three models is correct.
“In your Command phase, one or more CHAOS KNIGHTS units from your army can make a Malefic Surge.”
“In your Command phase” is your turn only. Surges made at other times come from Profane Symbiosis, which has its own timing.
“one or more CHAOS KNIGHTS units from your army”. It correctly leaves out the allied Nurglings (Faction: Legiones Daemonica).

This is the Rules Update wording (Faction Pack 1.2, “Change Unnatural Fortitude to: ‘When this unit is selected as the target of an attack, select one of the following to apply until the end of the phase: ▪ Models in this unit have a 5+ invulnerable save. ▪ Models in this unit have the Feel No Pain 6+ ability.’”). The line keeps the Empowered condition and the “or” (a choice the player makes) and the duration.

“Diabolic Power: When this unit is selected to shoot or fight, select either the [LETHAL HITS] or [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability. Until the end of the phase, weapons equipped by models in this unit have the selected ability.” The pick offers both options, kind all (all weapons), with the Empowered condition and the duration.
“WHEN: End of any phase.” That is all five phases (invariants.js: an “End of any phase” WHEN names every phase).
“End of any phase”, with no player named, so either turn.
“TARGET: One CHAOS KNIGHTS unit from your army that is not Empowered.” Not being Empowered is a game state, so it stays in the gist rather than in needs.

The target, effect and restriction are literal: “not Empowered”, “makes a Malefic Surge”, “cannot select the same unit … more than once per battle round”. But the WHEN “End of any phase.” is lost on the row. stratWhenShort adds “End of” only when shortWhen is not “Any phase”, and with all five phases at turn either shortWhen is “Any phase”. So the row reads “Any phase” and the gist alone can carry the moment that decides when it can be used.

fix.gist: End of any phase: your unit that is not Empowered makes a Malefic Surge (not the same unit more than once per battle round).

This is the Rules Update Effect (Faction Pack 1.2: “‘Until the attacking unit has finished making its attacks, each time an attack targets your unit, worsen the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 1.’”). The line has Fight phase, AP worsened by 1, and “until that enemy unit has attacked”, which is the same duration.

It keeps the WHEN/TARGET trigger (“just after an enemy unit has selected its targets” with your unit among them) and the updated EFFECT word for word in short form. The row's “Fight · Either turn” gives the phase.
“WHEN: Your Command phase, just after a CHAOS KNIGHTS CHARACTER unit from your army makes a Malefic Surge.”
“Your Command phase.”
“That CHAOS KNIGHTS CHARACTER unit.” Every Knight in this list is a CHARACTER (NR Categories), and the Nurglings are excluded.

The EFFECT part is literal (“Select one objective marker your unit is within range of that you control … until your opponent’s Level of Control … is greater than yours at the end of a phase”). But the WHEN trigger “just after a CHAOS KNIGHTS CHARACTER unit from your army makes a Malefic Surge” decides when it can be used, and it is dropped. The row shows only “Your Command”, so it reads as usable at any point of the Command phase by any Knight. The fix adds the trigger, as the Hellforged and Bulwark gists keep their “Just after …”.

fix.gist: Just after your unit makes a Malefic Surge: select one objective marker you control that your unit is within range of; it stays under your control until your opponent’s Level of Control over it is greater than yours at the end of a phase.
